changes.before: Complete read_note(path). Open the UTF-8 text file for reading and return its complete text unchanged. Use a with block so the file closes after reading. The exercise supplies existing readable files; do not swallow missing-file errors.
changes.after: Read a UTF-8 note and return all the text from read().

before: A file keeps data outside a running function. Its path tells Python which file to open.
open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") opens a text file for reading. The encoding describes how stored bytes become characters.

A with block manages cleanup when its block finishes.
```python
with open("demo-note.txt", "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    text = handle.read()
print(text)
```
The name handle refers to the open file during the block. read() returns all remaining text, including line breaks.
This example needs a demo-note.txt file in the working directory. A relative path starts there; it is not automatically relative to whichever editor tab is open.
After the block, the file is closed even if reading raised an exception. The returned text remains usable because it is a separate string.
Reading mode does not erase the file. Writing mode "w" can replace existing contents, so do not use it for this reading task.
An empty file contains the empty string. That differs from a missing file, which raises an error.
The supplied practice files live in the app’s isolated runner filesystem. They are not direct access to files elsewhere on your device.
Return the text exactly: do not strip spaces or line breaks when the requirement is to preserve the note.
